correctness.rationale: Stationary mixture [1], independently checked for normalization, yields the exact Gaussian-maximum CDF. The centered Gaussian maximum has the stated Gumbel limit. Separate endpoint coordinate changes give powers L^{-alpha} and L^{-beta}, integrable dominating bounds justify both limits and the rare-event conditional environmental laws. Mills estimates with a moving logarithmic threshold give the lower raw endpoint factor (log L/L)^alpha; uniform small-tail approximation plus the Gamma integral give the upper raw factor L^{-beta-1/2}. A standalone checker replayed 66 integral/numerical assertions; finite checks are not an infinite proof. All assumptions, constants and excluded degenerate parameter limits are explicitly stated.

value.rationale: The source discovers a finite limiting support for the maximum despite unbounded particle positions. Quantifying the actual finite-N probability of violating that apparent support is a motivated physical and mathematical gap, not an arbitrary finite-order moment. Different logarithmic powers and the extra log-log versus inverse-square-root-log asymmetry identify distinct endpoint mechanisms, while rare-event posterior laws localize the shared environment and may inform extreme-event diagnostics. No claim of finite-sample experimental feasibility is made.
